Synopsis:
Dialog featuring a goblin and half-orc. Triggers the start of the caravan escort with the Drider appearing.The Drider is male, half-drow elf and half spider (bottom half). He carries a magical lantern to ward off the shadows

Cluster Contexts:
- SCL_Drider_CaravanStart.json: Before the scene the caravan camp has been ambushed off‑screen: most of the goblin worshippers are dead and only a few survivors remain. The Drider (Kar'niss) arrives, inspects the slaughtered goblins, and speaks with suspicion and anger toward the player, implying he holds someone present to account (he even addresses a figure as "Majesty"). A handful of faithful goblins have survived and will become the caravan's remaining followers to escort. The Drider carries a magical lantern that wards shadows—an important tool for the coming caravan escort that this dialog initiates.
- SCL_Drider_HarpersAndPlayersAmbush.json: The players have agreed to help the Harpers ambush a caravan of Absolute cultists and prisoners. You've just arrived at the ambush site - the mood is tense, words are spoken in harsh whispers. When the Caravan arrives there's a monsterous drider at its head, muttering to itself, talking to an imaginary queen/majesty that represents the voice of his God, The Absolute. The player can try to trick the drider into handing over its magic lantern (the Moonlantern - a glowing lantern hanging from the end of a staff), although that could leave the drider exposed to the worst effects of the curse. Will likely end in combat, either because you signaled the Harpers to spring their ambush or because the drider got suspicious and attacked.

If you have, you can play it and the drider will emerge. If you haven't, they can tell you where to find it.

context: The caravan camp has just been ambushed off‑screen: most of the goblin worshippers are dead and only a few survivors remain to act as the remaining escort. Kar'niss, a male drider (half‑drow, half‑spider) arrives, inspects the slaughter, and speaks angrily and suspiciously—even addressing an imagined "Majesty" as if answering a deity or command. He carries a glowing Moonlantern that wards shadows, an important tool for the forthcoming caravan escort and a potential focal point of conflict. The mood is tense: the players are at an ambush site (they may be working with the Harpers), and Kar'niss’s hostility toward those present could lead to interrogation, trickery over the lantern, or combat.
